title: Understanding fishing as a ‘way of life’
summary: Written for World Fisheries Day: planners and policy makers need to understand fishing as a way of life, not only as a means of exploiting aquatic resources.

title: The future of Sri Lanka’s lobster and giant freshwater prawn sector
summary: How consumers choose between lobster and giant freshwater prawn, the problems fishers face, and the case for eco-labelling and traceability.

title: Financial inclusion to build economic resilience among women fish processors in South Sri Lanka
summary: Reports on the Savings for Future workshops in Kudawella and the “Seettu Samagam” approach to savings for women fish processors.

title: Oceans silenced, communities whipped: Energy crisis on fisheries
summary: The 2022 fuel crisis kept fishers ashore and pushed fish prices past Rs. 3,000/kg, cutting families off from their main source of protein.

title: Towards a new area of support for small-scale fisheries and aquaculture
summary: Regional closing event of the International Year of Artisanal Fisheries and Aquaculture 2022 for Asia, Bangkok, with SLFSSF among the panel.

title: Decent work for fishers: Towards ratifying the ILO Work in Fishing Convention 188
summary: Offshore and deep-sea fishing changed labour relations on board. Sri Lanka has yet to ratify the convention that protects fishing crews.
